content.thinking:
I'm planning the kitsune design in full before writing any code, since I won't be able to iterate: a fox standing with a shoulder height around 0.8m, nine fanned tails each tipped with a flame-like glow, and a coordinate system facing +Z with left as +X.

Building the skeleton hierarchy...

I'll keep the body as one sweep bound to the spine chain, with the neck as a separate sweep narrowing from 0.1 to 0.085, and head parts attached to the head joint. For the body loft I'm defining width/height stations running from the rump to the chest, then painting with a cel-shaded fur edge for the white belly and coat.

For the color scheme, I'm leaning toward a classic white kitsune look: cream-white fur (#fff6ea), crimson markings (#d8283a), gold ornaments (#f2b632), and cyan-violet flame accents on the tail tips, since that reads as more iconic than an orange fox palette, with cel shading handling the shadow tones on the white coat.

Now I'm figuring out how to paint the markings as a custom function that returns red stripes along the flank versus white elsewhere, feeding that into the cel shader as the lit color so shadows compute correctly on the patterned coat. I'm also adding dark indigo sock markings on the lower legs using a position-based check, nesting paints so the coat function conditionally returns different color strings depending on where on the body it's sampling.

Still writing coat markings...

Now I'm setting up the leg rig, placing shoulder and foot targets for the front limbs using the limb solver.

Now I'm working out the hind leg geometry, defining hip, knee, hock, and paw joints with three segments bending digitigrade-style, and naming each joint accordingly.

For the leg skin I'm setting up a sweep mesh with tapering radius values across the chain, then adding a small sphere for the paw attached to the tip joint.

Now I'm building the head: a skull sphere scaled to shape at the head bone, positioned using local directional offsets, then starting a snout frustum extending forward from the head.

Placing fang cones on the upper jaw, I'm uncertain whether the positioning API uses "left" or "right" keys consistently, so I'll compute coordinates directly from the head's world position with a small offset helper for symmetry instead of relying on ambiguous side keys.

Now the neck pitches down slightly into the head joint, and I'm shaping the ears as sharp triangular extrusions leaning outward from the skull, being careful the outline doesn't self-intersect.

Working out the inner ear positioning now, offset slightly forward and up from the outer ear with a smaller red-colored extrude...

I'm also planning gold torus rings as earring accents near the ear base.

Now I'm working on the eye decals: using golden iris color with red kumadori accents, positioning them via angled azimuth/elevation on the skull surface with mirroring for symmetry.

Still mapping out marking points...

For the forehead mark I'll add a diamond decal using an SVG teardrop shape in red with a gold inner dot, placed and oriented via a direction and up vector. Then for the cheeks I'm planning fur tuft textures as flame-shaped white decals scattered around.

Scattering fur tuft cards across the neck and chest, filtering by orientation so they only cluster on the lower neck sweep like a ruff.

Now I'm adding cheek tufts by scattering from the skull sides based on normal direction, then moving on to the nine tails -- defining a tail base joint at the hip's rear and planning a fan arrangement where each tail branches at an angle spread across the group.

For each tail I'm computing a horizontal spread angle and elevation that's highest at center and lower at the edges, then building curved path points from the base outward with an upward curl near the tips.

Checking the overall bounding dimensions look reasonable, then working through tail segment naming so each joint gets a unique identifier in the chain hierarchy without collisions.

I'll switch to explicit naming per tail and segment index to avoid ambiguity, using a catmull-rom path through the four points for smooth curvature across three spans. For the radius profile I'm settling on a bushy taper that widens in the middle and tapers to a point at the tip, with a gradient coloring that could include a distinct tip band.

For the tip coloring I'll use a gradient from white to a light cyan sampled along the latter portion of the path, giving an icy highlight at the end. Then I'm adding glowing flame-like cards at the tail tip, oriented along the tangent frame, using a flame texture with cyan outer glow and white inner core to give a spirit-fire effect.

I can combine multiple tails' frames into a single cards call for efficiency, applying spin variation across repeated frame sets for a layered double-flame look, then boosting the glow strength. I'll also scatter a handful of small floating wisp orbs around the fox at varying heights and radii, each topped with a tiny flame glow, to add some ambient magical floating effects.

Each wisp pairs a small glowing sphere with a flame card cluster rising from it, bound to a nearby joint like the hips for deterministic movement, and I'm positioning them off to the sides and ahead of the fox to avoid overlapping the tails. For the collar, I'm sweeping a gold-and-red shimenawa-style rope loop around the neck using a surface sweep anchored at a neck joint, lifting it slightly off the mesh to avoid clipping.

Working out rope loop angles...

Calculating ring sizing...

I'll settle on roughly 0.123 radius with a thin gold tube for each of the nine tails, giving each its own rim. For the chest, I'm planning a red obi-style band looped around the waist at the spine joint, tied with gold, tilted to match the bone axis rather than sitting flat.

Now I'm adding kumadori-style red flank markings using swept drape paths along curved shoulder and hip points, wrapped in a reusable marks function, plus a dorsal zigzag stripe painted along the back and some flame-card accents near the shoulders.

For the flame details, I'm scattering small glowing flame cards along the upper spine using a filtered surface-hit approach, then adding similar tiny flames at each ankle by sampling points along the leg chains and orienting the cards with an upward frame, relying on nearest-joint weighting since no explicit bone is assigned.

On texture reuse: I'm keeping it simple by using a single teal flame texture across all these card batches rather than introducing a second tint or texture for variety, since multiple calls with the same texture just produce separate meshes that I can glow uniformly afterward.

Writing SVG code...

Adding cheek hair tufts and chest ruff scatter cards based on body surface normals. I'm settling on a deep indigo sock color for the legs, keeping coat continuity between head, body, and sock materials so paw spheres match the leg paint logic.

For the front legs only, I'm adding small gold anklet torus rings near the paw position, oriented with the leg's bend, while skipping anklets on the hind legs since their lower segment slants differently.

Setting up imports and scaffolding...

Still defining coat zones...

The tail's gradient coloring uses a separate paint function, and I'm checking that the chain-building logic for the spine correctly inherits from the hips joint, with the rump positioned beyond the spine's starting point.

Checking the hind leg attachments to the hips and confirming the body skinning follows the spine joints correctly, since legs rigidly parent to hips which itself is a spine child. The neck joints chain off the last spine joint with a sweep using tapering radii, and I'm considering whether to add a chest sphere to bulk out that area near the loft's widest station.

Now working out head placement using helper coordinates relative to the head joint position—sizing the skull larger than the neck's end radius for a fox-like silhouette with a ruff, then placing the snout, nose tip, cheek fluff, and lower jaw as separate spheres offset from that same head anchor point.

For the jaw, I'm defining a joint parented to the head with forward/down offsets for aim, then adding a dark red sphere for the mouth interior sized to fit the sliver gap between the snout's lower edge and the jaw's top. Now I'm positioning two fangs on the upper jaw symmetrically offset to each side.

For the ears I'm sketching an outline with three points, one sharp, giving thickness and smoothing, then placing it on the head with a slight tilt and mirrored x-offset for symmetry between left/right ears. I'm setting up cel-shaded coloring on the ear extrusion, with a darker tip toward the back using a position-based paint function.

Now I'm adding inner ear detail in pink, plus planning gold torus earrings with hanging red tassels, a forehead mark decal, whiskers, and eye textures using an anime-style iris.

For the eyes, I'm using the skull surface to find hit points for placement, sizing the decals around 0.058 by 0.08 to fit the sphere's proportions. I'm also considering a neck rope loop around the neck tube as another accessory.

Writing the gold bell and sweep code...

Adding a thin gold loop near the hips and skipping extra chest ornaments, then writing code to generate the nine tail segments with angular offsets and positions based on symmetric index spacing...

Still writing tail geometry...

Checking tail separations to confirm neighboring tails don't overlap, and verifying tail bases stay clear of the hind legs and rear body geometry. Now I'm setting up the chain call to build each tail from its spline points, parented to the tail base.

Sweeping each tail chain with a tapering radius profile toward a flame-shaped tip, then setting up flame frames near the tip for attaching small card elements with slight spin and lean variation along a default flow direction.

Adding gold and red ring parts positioned along the tail path with specific torus dimensions, orienting them using the tangent direction at their joints, then finishing with a small-radius tip cap so the flame tapers cleanly at the end.

Now I'm scattering small flame cards along the body tube surface, filtering by normal direction and position so they only appear on the upper spine area, then setting up wisp elements with glowing cyan-white spheres and crossed flame cards oriented along their frames at several scattered positions.

I'm also checking that the tail and wisp placements stay within a reasonable overall model extent, then defining a fur tuft texture using an SVG path with a cream fill and soft tan stroke sized for crisp rendering.

Now I'm scattering fur card clusters across the chest, neck, and cheeks—filtering hit points by normal direction and position to target the ruff and tuft regions, then setting size, lean, and bend parameters for each cluster to get natural-looking fur growth patterns.

I'm skipping tail tufts since the gradient shading already handles those, and simplifying the flame placement at each paw by just using fixed foot positions with small glowing card sizes near the ground.

For the hind legs, I'm adding thigh spheres at the hips with scaled dimensions to bulk up the haunch, plus similar shoulder spheres at the front. I'm defining the limb function with root position, segment lengths, and bend directions so the leg geometry reaches naturally from hip to foot without overextending.

Now I'm wiring up the leg chains—naming each joint (shoulder, elbow, paw for front; hip, knee, ankle, paw for hind) and attaching them to the spine's last joint so they follow the body properly.

Now I'm adding the kumadori markings—red arcs draping across the face, flank, and haunch, positioning them against the body surface and defining tapered sweep geometry for each drape.

I'm naming the tail base joint and double-checking the ink color gets reused for claws and the nose, with white for whiskers. I'm now sketching tiny toe details on each paw—small bumps or spheres to suggest claws without overcomplicating the geometry.

Now I'm working out the whisker rods, positioning them so they angle outward and back from each side of the face.

For the forehead, I'm adding a gold ornament — thinking through whether a crescent or ring decal works best, then planning a beaded gold necklace trail that follows a loop path around the neck.

Now I'm positioning a decal mark on the skull's forehead, aiming the direction and up vectors so it sits naturally above the skull center, with a size that fits proportionally. I'm also checking that the glow effect applies properly to the card meshes at the right intensity.

Checking that paw and leg bottoms rest right at floor level so nothing clips or floats, then moving to the tail sweep geometry—defining the color gradient along the sweep path and making sure flame-like card frames orient along the tail's tangent near its tip.

Working out typing for frame arrays and figuring out how to satisfy the Frame/FrameInput type requirements for chain points without import conflicts, then finalizing all the pieces to write the full file.

Checking the along callback's return type is fine since void-returning positions accept value-returning arrows, and body parts get bound to the spine bone.
